etymologies.etymologyHTML: From the Scots dialect of English meaning "legally pertinent," used in Scots legal circles starting in the early 1500s. Borrowed from Latin relevāns, relevāntem, present active participle of relevō (“lift up again, lighten, relieve”), from re- (“again”) + levō (“lift”).

definitions.definition: (especially) Directly related, connected, or pertinent, with important ramifications or implications.
Related, connected, or pertinent to a topic.

quote.citation: 1973 December 20, “Hansen says Christmas time for thanks, hope”, in The Aberdeen Times‎[1]:
quote.text: The message of Christmas is still relevant as we near the end of a troubled year and the beginning of an uncertain but challenging new year.

quote.citation: 2008, Scott Cooper, Fritz Grutzner, Birk Cooper, Tips and Traps for Marketing Your Business‎[2], McGraw-Hill, →ISBN, page 39:
quote.text: Motorola was quickly losing the cell-phone battle to Nokia for a time. When they launched the RAZR phone and combined it with their "Hello Moto" campaign, it made the brand relevant again.

definitions.definition: (slang, by extension) Famous, popular, or noteworthy in a contemporary context.
